evals.expected_output: Lists every workload in the supplied workload context with its name, shape, region, and account exactly as supplied, without substituting an invented numeric account ID.
assertions: The output reports each workload's account value exactly as supplied in the context, without substituting an invented numeric account ID

evals.expected_output: Identifies orders-api as the first workload and proposes an artifact name of the form sustainability-review-orders-api-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md.

evals.prompt: List the six focus areas of the AWS Well-Architected Sustainability Pillar that this skill assesses, with the number of best practices in each. State the total. No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Lists SUS01 Region Selection (1), SUS02 Alignment to Demand (6), SUS03 Software and Architecture Patterns (5), SUS04 Data Patterns (8), SUS05 Hardware and Services (4), SUS06 Development and Deployment (5), totalling 29 best practices.
assertions: contains 'SUS01' or contains 'SUS 1' or contains 'Region Selection'
contains 'SUS02' or contains 'SUS 2' or contains 'Alignment to Demand'
contains 'SUS04' or contains 'SUS 4' or contains 'Data Patterns'

evals.prompt: A customer says: 'We migrated 40 TB from S3 Standard to Glacier Deep Archive last quarter, but our reported carbon emissions went UP. Did our optimization fail?' Answer using the skill's guidance. No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Explains that reported emissions cannot be attributed to the storage change. Checks the carbon model version first — against whatever figure the customer published previously, since the API restates all history under one version and cannot signal a revision internally — then grid carbon intensity, AWS-side infrastructure changes, allocation share shifts, and scope/LBM-vs-MBM composition, before considering actual usage. States that a storage reduction not showing up in reported emissions is the expected outcome, and that the resource intensity KPI is the attributable measure.
assertions: contains 'model version' or contains 'ModelVersion' or contains 'methodology'
contains 'LBM' or contains 'MBM' or contains 'location-based' or contains 'market-based'
contains 'expected' or contains 'not a regression' or contains 'did not fail'

evals.prompt: For our carbon footprint review I need the last 12 months of AWS carbon emissions, ending this month. Which AWS Sustainability API operation would you call, what value must TimePeriod.Start have and why, what rule decides which months come back in the response, and will the current month return data? No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Names sustainability:GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions. States TimePeriod.Start must be the first day of a month at midnight (YYYY-MM-01T00:00:00Z) or that month is silently excluded, that selection is half-open so a month M is returned only when Start <= M-01T00:00:00Z < End (an End falling exactly on a month's first instant excludes that month), and that the current month returns no data because emissions publish one month in arrears — a month's data is published by the 21st of the following month.
assertions: contains 'arrears' or contains 'lag' or contains 'one month' or contains 'delay' or contains '21st' or contains 'following month'

evals.prompt: A customer wants water data for their workload broken down by month, and says 'tell us what to change to reduce it.' Answer using the skill's guidance. No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Names sustainability:GetEstimatedWaterAllocation. States a monthly breakdown is not possible because only YEARLY_CALENDAR granularity is supported, so the figure is annual, in cubic metres (m3). States water is reporting-only — there is no water-specific Well-Architected best practice and no water KPI, so no recommendation is derived from it; the levers that reduce it are the same efficiency levers already in the review. Notes the figure is water withdrawn (not consumed) and covers AWS data center operations only, excluding water embodied in upstream electricity generation.
assertions: contains 'reporting' or contains 'disclosure' or contains 'no water-specific' or contains 'not a KPI'

evals.expected_output: States that instance counts are not acceptable because instance types differ in size, and that the correct measure is vCPU-hours (vCPU count x running hours), split into provisioned and utilized. Names ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes (VCpuInfo.DefaultVCpus) as the authoritative vCPU source and notes the KPI is normalized against business output.
assertions: contains 'vCPU-hour' or contains 'vCPU hour' or contains 'vCPU-hours'
contains 'business output' or contains 'per transaction' or contains 'normali'

evals.expected_output: States that the skill must not invent a business output metric. It uses the first available Step 1 fallback denominator — request count, then invocation count, then data processed — and states that fallback's caveat; if none is available it reports absolute resource footprint only, because intensity KPIs cannot be computed without a denominator. SUS06-BP01 (communicate and cascade sustainability goals: no sustainability KPI defined for the workload) becomes a finding, and it is the top recommendation when no business output metric can be established.
assertions: contains 'not invent' or contains 'never invent' or contains 'do not invent' or contains 'fabricat'

evals.prompt: Explain why cost is not always a reliable proxy for a workload's sustainability footprint. Give at least three specific mechanisms where cost and resource consumption diverge. No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Names at least three of: volume discounts / Savings Plans / Reserved Instances reduce spend without reducing resource consumption; free inbound data transfer consumes resources with no cost signal; regional price and grid carbon intensity are set by unrelated mechanisms; growth can improve cost-per-unit while absolute consumption rises; committed-but-idle capacity has no marginal cost signal.
assertions: contains 'discount' or contains 'Savings Plan' or contains 'Reserved'

evals.prompt: Why does the skill treat reported carbon emissions as context rather than as the customer's sustainability score? Name the specific factors that move a reported MTCO2e figure independently of anything the customer does, and say what that implies about attributing an emissions change to a customer action. No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Explains that a reported figure is confounded: methodology revisions (history is restated under the current model version), grid carbon intensity variation, AWS renewable energy procurement landing in Scope 2 MBM, data center efficiency and hardware refresh, allocation-share shifts caused by other customers' usage, and reporting lag plus the 0.5 g reporting threshold all move the number on their own and at the same time as the customer's changes. Concludes that a period-over-period change cannot be attributed to a customer action until those causes are ruled out (Step 8), so emissions are presented as context while resource intensity KPIs — which have no such confounders — are the attributable assessment. Must NOT claim a specific percentage of the footprint is outside customer control, and must NOT say customer action is immaterial: provisioning determines how much AWS infrastructure is allocated to the account and Region choice is SUS01-BP01.
assertions: contains 'model version' or contains 'ModelVersion' or contains 'methodology'
The output does not state a specific percentage or proportion of the footprint as being outside the customer's control
The output does not claim that customer action such as rightsizing or decommissioning is immaterial to the reported footprint

evals.prompt: The role has sustainability:GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions but NOT sustainability:GetEstimatedWaterAllocation, so the water call returns AccessDeniedException. What does the skill do? No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: States that the review continues and produces a full report. Carbon and water are separately authorized and requested independently, so the water denial does not suppress the carbon data: the emissions context section is reported normally, the water sub-section is omitted, and the report names the missing IAM action. The SUS01-SUS06 assessment and resource intensity KPIs are unaffected because this data is enrichment, not a prerequisite.
assertions: contains 'enrichment' or contains 'not a prerequisite' or contains 'not required'

evals.prompt: A user asks this skill to produce a right-sizing table recommending a specific smaller instance type for each of their 40 EC2 instances. How should the skill respond? No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: States that per-instance right-sizing is out of scope and belongs to AWS Compute Optimizer. The skill reports the provisioned-versus-utilized gap at fleet or workload level (SUS05-BP01) and refers the user to Compute Optimizer for individual instance sizing.
assertions: contains 'fleet' or contains 'architecture' or contains 'workload level'

evals.prompt: List the five severity levels the skill uses for findings, in order from most to least urgent, and state what severity means in a sustainability review as opposed to an operational review. No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Lists CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO in that order, and states that severity reflects resource-footprint impact and remediation effort rather than operational risk - a CRITICAL sustainability finding is not an outage risk.
assertions: contains 'footprint' or contains 'not an outage' or contains 'not operational risk'

evals.prompt: Which of the 29 Well-Architected Sustainability best practices can this skill NOT assess from AWS APIs alone, and how must the report handle them? No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Identifies roughly four practices needing human input - SUS02-BP05 (team member resources / end-user devices), SUS03-BP04 (customer device impact), SUS06-BP05 (managed device farms), and SUS03-BP03 (code profiling) in part - and states they must be reported explicitly as NEEDS HUMAN INPUT rather than silently omitted or marked met, because a scorecard implying 29 of 29 coverage would be misleading.

evals.prompt: Before we let you run a sustainability review on our production AWS account: will the review change any AWS resources, and which categories of API calls does it never make? No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: States the skill is read-only throughout and never calls Modify*, Delete*, Terminate*, or Create* operations. Every recommendation is for a human to action.

evals.prompt: A customer runs 40 x86 m5.xlarge EC2 instances on Amazon Linux, an RDS for PostgreSQL 15 db.r5.large instance, an RDS for SQL Server instance, and Lambda .zip functions on x86_64 with the Python runtime. They ask: 'If we move everything to Graviton, how much CO2 will we save?' Answer using the skill's guidance. No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Does not give a CO2e figure or a percentage emissions saving. Quotes AWS's statement that Graviton-based EC2 instances use up to 60% less energy than comparable instances for the same performance, attributed to AWS and not applied to the customer's fleet. Explains that the effect on reported emissions cannot be predicted, because the methodology pools EC2 emissions in a cluster and allocates them by normalized instance-hours, and that impact is expressed as vCPU-hours moved to Graviton and tracked through compute intensity. Recommends the PostgreSQL instance class change and the Lambda arm64 switch first, with the EC2 fleet needing a compatibility check (Compute Optimizer migration effort or the transition guide). Marks the SQL Server instance as having no Graviton option. Notes m5 as a previous-generation family.
assertions: contains 'up to 60%' or contains 'performance per watt'
The output does not state a specific MTCO2e amount or a percentage reduction in the customer's carbon emissions
The output recommends moving the RDS for PostgreSQL instance or the Lambda functions before the self-managed EC2 fleet

evals.prompt: During a sustainability review of the orders-api workload in account 123456789012, the topology and CloudWatch data show an EC2 fleet provisioning about 30,000 vCPU-hours per month. GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions for the same account returned 12 complete months in which every emissions type — the LBM and MBM totals and every Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 series — is 0.0 MTCO2e. The customer says: 'So our AWS footprint is basically nothing.' How does the skill handle this in the review, and how should the findings express the impact of its recommendations? No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Runs the emissions sanity check: every emissions type, LBM and Scope 3 included, is zero in months where the topology shows about 30,000 provisioned vCPU-hours, so the emissions data and the topology describe different scopes (most often emissions retrieved for a different account than the one the topology covers, or sample data). Reports that scope mismatch as an explicit finding instead of reconciling, averaging or explaining it away, and states that the emissions figure cannot be read as this workload's footprint. Notes that zero or absent values mean below the reporting threshold, not zero impact, and that near-zero Scope 2 MBM can be normal but LBM and Scope 3 should still reflect a fleet of this size. Does not tell the customer the footprint is tiny or negligible. Keeps the resource intensity KPIs as the assessment and states every recommendation's impact in resource terms (vCPU-hours, weighted GB-months, GB transferred), never in MTCO2e.
assertions: contains 'different scope' or contains 'scope mismatch' or contains 'mismatch'
contains 'threshold' or contains 'not zero impact' or contains 'not the same as no impact'

The output reports the mismatch between the all-zero emissions data and the ~30,000 provisioned vCPU-hours/month in the topology as a finding, stating that the two inputs cover different scopes, rather than explaining the zeros away
The output does not describe the workload's footprint as tiny, negligible, near zero or nothing, and does not agree with the customer that it is
The output does not state any recommendation's impact in MTCO2e; impact is expressed in resource terms such as vCPU-hours

evals.prompt: A customer published 412.7 MTCO2e (location-based, TOTAL_LBM_CARBON_EMISSIONS) as its FY2025 AWS footprint, covering January to December 2025, taken from the AWS Sustainability console when an earlier carbon model version was current. Today GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions for the same twelve months returns a location-based total of 468.3 MTCO2e, with ModelVersion v3.0.1 on every month. The customer did no optimization work. They ask: 'Why does AWS now show a different number for the same year? Did our footprint regress? And can you pull the figure under the old model so we can compare?' Answer using the skill's guidance. No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Checks the methodology version first (Step 8, cause 1). The API restates all history under the current model, so every month in the response carries the same ModelVersion (v3.0.1) and comparing ModelVersion across months can never reveal a revision. The right comparison is between v3.0.1 and the earlier version behind the published FY2025 figure; because they differ, the published number was restated under the current model — the change is in the instrument, not the workload — and the walkthrough stops there. States plainly that this is not a regression and is not attributable to the customer. Explains that the API cannot return the earlier version's figure for the same months; seeing the same months under different model versions needs Data Exports, which keeps each version separately (partitioned by model_version), but only for an export that already existed before the revision, and is read from S3 with Athena under a different permission set. Records v3.0.1 in the report and compares like with like (location-based against location-based).
assertions: The output checks the methodology (model) version change first and concludes the difference comes from restatement under the current model, not from a change in the workload
The output explains that the API restates all months under the current model version, so it cannot return the figure under the earlier version and every month carries the same ModelVersion
The output compares the current ModelVersion with the version behind the customer's published FY2025 figure, rather than comparing ModelVersion values across months of the API response
The output does not call the change a regression and does not attribute it to the customer's usage

evals.prompt:
During a sustainability review of account 123456789012, GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions succeeded, but GetEstimatedWaterAllocation failed with: 'Unexpected error: the request could not be completed.' The user then attached water-withdrawals-2024-2025.csv, exported from the AWS Sustainability console:

```csv
usage_year,usage_account_id,service,region,total_water_withdrawals_value,unit,model_version
2024,123456789012,Amazon EC2,eu-west-1,182.4,m3,v1.0.0
2024,123456789012,Amazon S3,eu-west-1,21.7,m3,v1.0.0
2025,123456789012,Amazon EC2,eu-west-1,169.9,m3,v1.0.0
2025,123456789012,Amazon S3,eu-west-1,23.1,m3,v1.0.0
```

They ask: 'Use this for the water section, show us the monthly trend, tell us whether our water use improved, and what we should change to cut it. Also, which IAM permission should we add so the API works next time?' Answer using the skill's guidance. No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Uses the attached CSV as the water source and keeps carbon from the API, stating the two different sources. Labels the water figures as user-provided rather than API-sourced, naming the file, the years covered and water model version v1.0.0. Reports annual totals per year (2024: 204.1 m3, 2025: 193.0 m3) in cubic metres, states that no monthly trend is possible because water is annual only, and does not divide the annual figures into months. States that the figure is water withdrawn, not consumed, and covers AWS data center operations only, excluding water embodied in upstream electricity generation. Derives no finding, KPI or recommendation from water — it is reported for disclosure only — and does not attribute the year-over-year difference to the customer, because water is allocated top-down with the same confounders as carbon. Records the API failure message verbatim and, because it is not an AccessDeniedException, recommends no IAM change and names no missing permission.
assertions: contains 'user-provided' or contains 'user provided' or contains 'user-supplied'
The output states that the figure is water withdrawn rather than consumed, and that it covers AWS data center operations only, excluding water embodied in upstream electricity generation
The output uses the attached CSV for water, reports it by year only, and does not produce or approximate a monthly water trend
The output derives no finding, KPI or recommendation from the water figures and does not attribute the 2024-to-2025 change to the customer's actions
The output does not recommend an IAM change or name a missing permission for the water API failure, because the failure was not an AccessDeniedException

evals.prompt: Today is 9 November 2026. A user signed in to their AWS Organizations management account asks, as part of a sustainability review: 'Show our carbon footprint emissions for the last 12 months broken down by linked account and by service, including this month so far.' State which AWS API call you would make and with which GroupBy dimensions, which services will appear as separate lines, what granularity and data availability to expect for this month and last month, and what a member account would see if it ran the same request. No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Calls sustainability:GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions, paginated, with Granularity MONTHLY, a TimePeriod.Start on the first of a month at midnight, and GroupBy USAGE_ACCOUNT_ID and SERVICE, giving a per-account breakdown because the management account covers more than one account; GetEstimatedCarbonEmissionsDimensionValues is optional, not a prerequisite. States that the service breakdown separates only Amazon EC2, Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront, with every other service reported under "Other", which cannot be split further. States that data is monthly and a month is published by the 21st of the following month: November 2026 is not available, and on 9 November October 2026 may not be published yet, so a missing recent month is a publication gap, not zero emissions. States that the management account sees consolidated data for member accounts for the periods they belonged to the organization, while a member account running the same request sees only its own data.
assertions: The output groups by both USAGE_ACCOUNT_ID and SERVICE and does not make GetEstimatedCarbonEmissionsDimensionValues a required step before the emissions call
The output states that only Amazon EC2, Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront are broken out by service and every other service is reported under Other
The output states that monthly data is published by the 21st of the following month, so November 2026 is not available and October 2026 may not be published yet on 9 November
The output states that a member account running the same request sees only its own data, while the management account sees the consolidated organization

evals.prompt: Partway through a sustainability review, at Step 7, read_skill_resource for references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md fails with: 'Error: resource not found: references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md'. Every other skill file loaded, and the topology, resource intensity KPIs and emissions data have already been collected. How does the skill handle this failure in the report, and how are the 29 best practices graded? No AWS access required.
evals.expected_output: Opens the report with a warning at the top — '⚠️ references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md could not be loaded: Error: resource not found: references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md' — quoting the error verbatim. Does not replace the checklist's evidence, NOT MET / PARTIAL criteria, severity rules and guards with general knowledge of the Well-Architected Sustainability Pillar, and does not grade from memory. Marks the practices that depend on the checklist NEEDS HUMAN INPUT rather than MET or NOT MET; the scorecard still lists all 29 and none is marked MET without evidence. Still completes the full report — resource intensity KPIs, emissions context and topology summary — because the skill always finishes.
assertions: The output puts the load failure, with the verbatim error message, at the top of the report
The output does not grade the affected practices from general knowledge of the Well-Architected Sustainability Pillar in place of the checklist's rules
The output still produces the full report, including the resource intensity KPIs, rather than stopping the review
